subject: Calculating joint fixed and random effects covariance "by hand"

messages.author: db6b7f5c26ead7f4
messages.subject: Calculating joint fixed and random effects covariance "by hand"
parts:
The sdreport() documentation describes the generalized delta-method for calculating the joint covariance matrix estimate for the random effects and fixed parameters. Is it possible to calculate this by hand from the MakeADFun() object? The main part of my question concerns the Jacobian matrix. This thread (https://groups.google.com/g/tmb-users/c/NLk0MPtg97U/m/JFcM3H4lAgAJ) mentions that there is a closed form solution for $J$ from the obj$he() function output, but doesn't elaborate. 

My main goal is to investigate how changes in $V(\hat(\theta))$ and $\hat{\theta}$ affect the  random effects in a given model.

messages.author: db6b7f5c26ead7f4
messages.subject: Re: Calculating joint fixed and random effects covariance "by hand"
parts:
With a little literature searching I found the answer for calculating J. In Skaug, H. J., & Fournier, D. A. (2006). Automatic approximation of the marginal likelihood in non-Gaussian hierarchical models. Computational Statistics & Data Analysis, 51(2), 699-709. The solution is the equation just above eqn (12). 

Now my question is more  related to the MakeADFun obj itself. If I have obj = MakeADFun(...,random="u",...) built, is there a way, e.g., through functions in env, etc., to find \hat{u} and the full hessian (for both fixed and random effects) for a different theta? Or, do I have to rebuild without the random statement.

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Re: Calculating joint fixed and random effects covariance "by hand"
parts:
I am not sure about this, but I am giving you my best guess.

1) When you say "  for a different theta " i think that can be controlled by the argument "par.fixed" to sdreport(), eg sdreport(obj,par.fixed = 70)
2) The objects you ask for are in the R code for sdreport(). In fact I think it is "A" in the line:                 term2 <- A %*% (Vtheta %*% t(A))

The code is not trivial to read. You find the mathematical notation in the help page for "sdreport":

page 24-25 of:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/TMB/TMB.pdf
